why: Pure Figma UI tour (toolbar, panels, frames, shapes) with no concept kids can't get from Gemini-built UI; whisper transcript is also badly looped.

title: Responsive Grid Systems In Web & UI Design

best.what: grid anatomy (rows, columns, gutter, margin) and the 5 grid types, plus mobile/tablet/desktop breakpoint numbers

why: The concept (column/gutter/margin, breakpoints, grid types) transfers straight to CSS layout even though it's demonstrated in Figma's layout-grid panel; transcript is garbled enough that a guide should restate the definitions.

title: Color Theory in UI Design

best.what: color wheel, warm/cool, and the naming of complementary/analogous/triadic/square/monochromatic + tint/shade/tone

why: Standard, correct color theory a kid can actually use when picking a palette in Gemini's output; concept doesn't depend on Figma.

title: Glassmorphism UI Design Tutorial for Beginners

title: TYPOGRAPHY PRINCIPLES: Typography Rules and Text Tool

best.what: typeface vs font, serif vs sans-serif, font weights/hierarchy for headings vs body

why: Clean, correct typography basics (hierarchy, serif/sans-serif, weight) that any web page needs; concept-first, not Figma-locked.

title: Figma Auto Layout | Master Auto Layout in 20 Minutes

best.what: auto layout = direction, gap, padding, fill vs hug, alignment on a pricing-card example (maps directly onto CSS flexbox)

why: Never says the word 'flexbox', but every setting shown (direction, gap, padding, grow/hug, align) is exactly flexbox reasoning kids will meet in CSS; a guide should make that bridge explicit.

title: Master Figma Components Properties, Variables & Variant Like a Pro!
why: Figma's own component/variant/instance-swap system, mechanically demonstrated with heavy repetition and unclear narration; the reusable-component idea is better taught where kids will actually build it (code).
